question.text: Let a plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> contain two lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>r</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi><mfenced><mrow><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi><mfenced><mrow><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mfenced><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> equals .......

solution.text:
Normal vector to the plane containing to given lines n→=i^j^k^11001-1=-i^+j^+k^

Direction ratios of normal vector =-1, 1, 1.

Equation of plane will be -1x-1+1y-0+1z-0=0

⇒ x-y-z-1=0

If x, y, z is foot of perpendicular drawn from M1, 0, 1 on the plane, then

⇒x-11=y-0-1=z-1-1=-1-0-1-13

⇒x=43, y=-13, z=23

⇒α+β+γ=43-13+23=53

⇒3α+β+γ=5.
